answer: On a knoll above the tide flats, each agent keeps one trellis panel and trains one vine on its wires. At low tide the agent walks out, ties one new shoot to the wire with a numbered twine tag, and reads the tide gauge on the end post. Tag number and tide height go in a logbook in a locked box at the gate. A warden checks each tag against its shoot and each reading against the gauge, and a copied tag or a faked reading costs the panel a season. A thousand fake names need a thousand tended panels, a thousand low-tide walks, and a thousand hand-tied tags.
